analyst_view.overall: Two sides near the bottom on 1 point each: Pafos are 31st and Midtjylland 34th after a 6-1 home defeat to Ajax on 5 Nov, so both need a win to stay in the play-off race. Each is without a player sent off last time: Pafos lose Lele (25% of their goal involvement, which the numbers already take off) and Midtjylland lose Kjell Watjen (two yellows against Ajax). Midtjylland, unbeaten and second in the Danish league level on points with FC Copenhagen, play at Brondby on Monday 23 Nov and at Copenhagen in a title clash on Sunday 29 Nov, so Mike Tullberg may rest players for this trip to Cyprus. Pafos (Ricardo Sa Pinto) are fourth in Cyprus and won 2-1 at Omonia Aradippou on 21 Nov; no referee is named yet and specific team news was thin.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already with Pafos cut about 19% for Lele's ban. I lean a little lower to about 2.4 because Midtjylland, wedged between Brondby away and the title clash at Copenhagen, are likely to rotate, which the numbers can't see. It is a mild lean; both teams' leaky recent defending is already in the momentum figures.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners and already add for both sides' high recent corner counts (Pafos conceded 52 in six). A rotated Midtjylland might sit deeper, which could cut both ways for corners, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 3.5 cards and already cut both sides about 9-10% for low recent card counts. Both teams just had a player sent off, Watjen for two yellows, but that is already reflected in the bans; no referee is named, so I stay at about 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots, 12.6 for Midtjylland. I trim to about 26.8 since a rotated away side with a big league game on Sunday is likely to take fewer shots; this schedule is not something the numbers count.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, already lifted for Pafos's sharp recent shooting and cut for Lele's ban. I lean slightly lower to about 9.4 for likely Midtjylland rotation.
